It does not say whether versions should be pinned. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: pip lock
contribution: Documents the experimental pip lock command, which writes pylock.toml by default and whose output is only guaranteed valid for the current Python version and platform. The page does not say that pip install consumes the file. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: Writing your pyproject.toml
contribution: Supports PyPA build-system recommendations and project metadata, including dynamic version and backend-specific metadata alternatives. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: pylock.toml specification
revision: lock-version 1.0, history entries April 2025 and March 2026
contribution: Defines pylock.toml as a format for reproducible installation in a Python environment, originally defined in PEP 751, and requires the file name pylock.toml or a named variant matching the pattern in the specification. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: pytest, good integration practices
contribution: Documents test discovery, test_*.py or *_test.py files, test prefixed functions and Test prefixed classes without an __init__ method, strongly suggests a src layout, and uses pip install -e . as the editable install step. It does not cover rootdir or conftest behavior. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: pytest, configuration
revision: scoped claims checked 2026-10-12, marks pytest.toml as added in 9.0
contribution: Supports pytest configuration precedence, pytest.toml added in 9.0, explicit config/rootdir options and fallback rules. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: pytest, CI pipelines
contribution: States that pytest detects CI when the CI or BUILD_NUMBER environment variable is set to a non empty value and then stops truncating the short test summary at the terminal width. Other effects are described as limited. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: Ruff, configuring Ruff
contribution: States that Ruff ignores a pyproject.toml without a [tool.ruff] section, that in one directory .ruff.toml takes precedence over ruff.toml and ruff.toml over pyproject.toml, that the closest configuration file is used for each file and settings are not merged across files, and that inheritance uses the extend field. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: Ruff, the Ruff linter
contribution: Supports explicit --fix behavior and the safe-fix default when fixing is requested. Running ruff check alone does not apply fixes. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: Ruff, the Ruff formatter
revision: scoped claims checked 2026-10-12, pre-commit example uses v0.17.0
contribution: Documents ruff format and ruff format --check, which does not write files and exits with 1 when a file would be reformatted. Describes the formatter as a drop in replacement for Black with known deviations. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: uv, project structure and files
contribution: States that uv requires pyproject.toml to identify the project root, keeps the environment in .venv next to it and advises against committing .venv, and that uv.lock is a cross platform, human readable TOML file that should be checked into version control and not edited manually. uv sync and uv run create or update the environment. Review scope: the linked factual claims in the five reviewed guides, checked on 2026-10-12. This is not a review of every page statement or project compatibility.

title: uv, using uv in Docker
contribution: Documents running a Python project in a Docker image with uv, installing dependencies in a layer before copying the project, uv sync --locked, and adding .venv to .dockerignore because the project environment depends on the local platform. It supports the works-with link only, not any project's Dockerfile.

title: React, using TypeScript
contribution: Documents TypeScript support for React, JSX and typed component props. Supports the React and TypeScript works-with link, without confirming a project's dependency versions or configuration.

title: TypeScript handbook, the basics
contribution: Explains static type checking and erasure of type annotations when producing JavaScript. Supports the separation of language checks and runtime behavior, not any application's correctness.

title: TypeScript handbook, everyday types
contribution: States that type assertions are removed at compile time and perform no runtime checking. Supports the warning that an assertion on an API payload does not validate that payload.

title: TypeScript TSConfig, noEmit
contribution: Documents that noEmit prevents JavaScript, declarations and source maps being emitted. Supports a possible separate type check, without asserting that a project's build already performs it.

title: Vitest, getting started
contribution: Documents Vite configuration reuse, dedicated Vitest configuration and a React example. Supports configuration discovery and the React works-with example, without imposing the current Vitest release on a project.

title: Vitest, command line interface
contribution: Documents vitest run as a single run without watch mode. Supports the distinction between a development watch session and a completed verification run.

title: Vitest, test environment
contribution: Documents Node as the default environment, jsdom and happy-dom as emulated browser environments, and Browser Mode as a separate option. Supports the environment distinction, not equivalence to a real device.

title: Playwright, best practices
contribution: Recommends user visible behavior, isolated tests, controlled data and role or other user facing locators. Supports browser test design and its limits, not a claim that every user journey is covered.

title: Playwright, emulation
contribution: Documents emulated viewport, touch, device parameters and color scheme. Supports explicit browser configuration, without treating emulation as an observed test on a physical phone.

title: W3C WAI, understanding keyboard access
contribution: Explains keyboard operability and the exception for functionality whose underlying input depends on the path of movement. Informs checks of the example's select and retry controls, not a whole product accessibility certification.

title: W3C WAI, understanding reflow
contribution: Explains reflow without loss of information or functionality at narrow equivalent viewport sizes, with exceptions for content requiring a two dimensional layout. Informs a responsive check rather than a blanket prohibition on table scrolling.

title: npm 11, npm ci
contribution: Supports npm 11 npm ci accepting package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json, rejecting mismatches and not rewriting lockfiles. Version-specific comparison with npm 12, not verified behavior in a project.

title: OpenAPI Specification, operation and security objects
contribution: Defines operation parameters, request bodies, responses and security requirements. Supports an interface description, not runtime enforcement or a claim that Atlas emits executable OpenAPI.

title: RFC 9110, HTTP semantics
contribution: Defines intended-effect idempotency, conditions for retrying non-idempotent requests and HTTP 202 acceptance without completed processing. Retry budgets and operation identifiers are project design recommendations.

title: MCP, tools specification
contribution: Defines tool input and optional output schemas and the trust limitation of tool annotations. Does not establish server approval, application authorization or configured MCP support.

title: OWASP, REST security cheat sheet
contribution: Recommends access control at every non-public REST endpoint. Atlas applies that guidance as a design question, without claiming the exported instructions enforce it.

title: Java SE 25, javac command
contribution: Documents compilation to JVM class files and --release targeting a supported language and platform API release. Does not prove third party compatibility or runtime input validity.

title: Spring Boot, system requirements
contribution: Lists Java minimum 17, compatibility through 26, explicit Maven support from 3.6.3 and possible higher third party requirements. These version facts are not selected defaults.

title: Spring Framework, controller validation
contribution: Explains controller argument and method Bean Validation, signature conditions and related errors. Validation is not caller authorization.

title: Spring Security, method security
contribution: States that the Boot security starter does not enable method-level authorization by default. The project must establish actual enabling and access rules.

title: Spring Framework, using Transactional
contribution: Documents default proxy interception and self-invocation limitations. Supports checking the actual transaction boundary, not an assumption that remote calls roll back.

title: Spring Boot, SQL databases
contribution: Documents JDBC and repository alternatives and DataSource configuration, including PostgreSQL DataSource support. Does not establish configured access or recommend one persistence abstraction universally.

title: Spring Boot, testing applications
contribution: Documents mock and running-server environments and the separation of client and server transactions. Test-side rollback does not clean up a server-side transaction.

title: Apache Maven, build lifecycle
contribution: Explains phase order and packaging or configured plugin bindings. Does not establish which tests a particular project discovers.

title: Apache Maven Failsafe, introduction
contribution: Documents separate integration-test and verify phases and recommends verify so cleanup and failure checking complete. No project plugin configuration is assumed.

title: Apache Maven Wrapper
contribution: Documents configured Maven distribution download and reuse. Reading it does not approve download sources, credentials or arbitrary build execution.

title: Apache Maven, using toolchains
contribution: Documents participating plugins using a build JDK independently of the JDK running Maven. Actual project configuration and versions remain to be established.

title: PostgreSQL, LIMIT and OFFSET
contribution: Explains unique ordering for predictable LIMIT and OFFSET subsets and the cost of skipped rows. Does not promise a stable snapshot across pages.

title: PostgreSQL, transaction isolation
contribution: Documents default Read Committed query snapshots and possible changes between successive SELECT statements. An API paging consistency policy is a separate design choice.

title: PostgreSQL, transactions tutorial
contribution: Explains all-or-nothing database transactions. Does not claim that a transaction undoes a separate remote service call or authorizes a write.

title: PostgreSQL, row security policies
contribution: Documents row restrictions when enabled, superuser and BYPASSRLS bypass and normal owner bypass. Actual application identity and policy behavior require tests.

title: PostgreSQL, backup and restore
contribution: Describes SQL dump, file system backup and continuous archiving as distinct approaches. Does not establish that any project has a usable or tested backup.

title: rea: README.md
contribution: Documents agent and CLI investigation of applications and binaries, with optional native analysis providers. Provider availability and completeness remain project-specific.

title: ghidra: README.md
contribution: Documents compiled-code disassembly, decompilation, graphing and scripting. Pseudocode and inferred signatures require inspection; no target was analyzed for Atlas.

title: Understand-Anything: README.md
contribution: Documents a generated code/knowledge graph, exploration, explanation and impact views. Completeness and cost require checks on the chosen repository.

title: Groma.md: README.md
contribution: Documents source scanning followed by curated C4 architecture stored as OKF Markdown. Scanner evidence is a starting point, not architectural authority.

title: serena: README.md
contribution: Documents semantic retrieval and editing at symbol level through an agent interface. Host and language support and any comparative benefit are not established here.

title: agent-reach: docs/README_en.md
contribution: Documents per-platform upstream access backends, setup levels and diagnostics. Platform and target content availability are separate from installation.

title: agent-reach: agent_reach/channels/web.py
contribution: Inspected WebChannel implementation returns an OK health status without a network probe and reads pages via Jina Reader. Atlas recommends checking actual returned target content.

title: laya: README.md
contribution: Documents typed choice, score and yes/no-style decisions and checkpoint routing. Accuracy, calibration and Atlas suitability require representative evaluation.

title: autoresearch: README.md
contribution: Documents an agent-driven single-GPU training experiment loop with a fixed training budget and evaluation metric. The generalized bounded-experiment procedure is Atlas guidance.

title: ponytail: skills/ponytail/SKILL.md
contribution: Documents reuse and minimal necessary implementation while preserving requested behavior, validation and relevant checks. Cost or quality benefits are not asserted.

title: spec-kit: README.md
contribution: Documents specification, bug-fixing and idea-assessment processes with reusable templates. These are optional process references, not an Atlas package format.

title: superpowers: README.md
contribution: Documents clarification, planning, implementation and review through composable skills. Its full opinionated process is not adopted as an Atlas requirement.

title: agentrc: README.md
contribution: Documents experimental repository-context generation and evaluation. Generated instructions and readiness scores are not proof of task performance.

title: apm: README.md
contribution: Documents manifests, locked agent dependencies and deployment to selected hosts. Atlas neither resolves these dependencies nor exports an APM package.

title: awesome-copilot: README.md
contribution: Documents a collection of agents, instructions, skills and plugins. Useful for discovery, with separate review of each chosen item.

title: anthropic-skills: README.md
contribution: Documents skill examples and explicitly distinguishes Apache-2.0 examples from source-available document skills. Reuse terms need per-item inspection.

title: microsoft-skills: README.md
contribution: Documents technical skills, agents and configuration examples, mainly for Azure and Microsoft AI Foundry. Stack applicability remains explicit.

title: OpenSpec: README.md
contribution: Documents change proposals, specifications, design, tasks and an archive workflow. Atlas does not install or execute OpenSpec from this reference.

title: OpenSpec: docs/existing-projects.md
contribution: Documents starting with the touched slice of an existing project and adding behavior deltas without a whole-system specification prerequisite.

title: OpenSpec: schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml
contribution: Documents proposal, specification, design and task artifacts, including behavior-delta conventions and scenario structure.

title: OpenSpec: skills/openspec-verify-change/SKILL.md
contribution: Documents separate completeness, correctness and coherence review, including implementation evidence rather than structural validation alone.

title: Marketing Skills, Customer Research procedure
contribution: Documents three research modes, extraction of tasks, pains, triggers and alternatives, theme and segment synthesis, and sample bias checks. Supports the scoped description of the source procedure. Does not establish representative customer preferences, comparative repository effectiveness or an executed Atlas workflow.

title: Knowledge Work Plugins, Synthesize Research procedure
contribution: Describes source-level observations, thematic synthesis, attributed evidence, frequency, impact, confidence, recommendations and open questions, with distinctions between findings and quotes. Supports the documented procedure contents, not configured connectors, valid population inference or successful execution.

title: Knowledge Work Plugins, Analyze procedure
contribution: Distinguishes a metric lookup, full analysis and formal report and describes data gathering, analysis, row count, null, magnitude, continuity and aggregation checks. Supports a source procedure description. Does not establish warehouse access, data quality or a verified business result.

title: Knowledge Work Plugins, Validate Data procedure
contribution: Provides methodology and calculation review prompts, including population and metric definitions, comparison fairness, join inflation, denominator changes and supported conclusions. Supports the factual account of these prompts, not the validity of every example or a certified analysis.

title: MADR, full decision record template
contribution: Defines context, considered options and outcome with optional drivers, consequences, confirmation and status metadata. Confirmation asks how implementation or compliance can be checked. Atlas's recommendation to make confirmation explicit is an adaptation, not a mandatory rule in the source template.

title: Backlog.md, task features and workflow documentation
contribution: Describes Markdown task files, task acceptance criteria, reusable Definition of Done items, milestones and dependencies. Supports the scoped documentation claim. Does not establish an installed version, configured task store or Atlas CLI or MCP integration.

title: Backlog.md, task finalization guide
contribution: Calls for evidence for acceptance and completion items, relevant tests, interaction checks, marking only proven items and recording the final summary before the terminal status. Supports these guide contents only. Reading this guide does not authorize task changes or establish an executed result.

title: Repomix: repository packing and scope controls
contribution: Documents repository packing, file and total token counts, include/exclude options and ignore-file behavior. Supports the optional packing step only, not context completeness or measured improvement.

title: Docling: supported document processing capabilities
contribution: Documents multiple-format parsing, PDF layout, reading order, table structure, OCR, DoclingDocument and export formats. Supplies options for an extraction trial without establishing corpus accuracy.

title: MarkItDown: Markdown conversion purpose and dependencies
contribution: Documents Markdown conversion for text analysis, high-fidelity conversion limits, and format-specific optional dependencies. Supports tool selection and prerequisite checks, not a conversion accuracy ranking.

title: Promptfoo: test-case configuration
contribution: Documents test-case variables, assertions, metadata, per-case repeats and provider filtering. Supports a configuration-based evaluation option without claiming scorer quality or benchmark results.

title: Inspect AI: evaluation task structure
contribution: Documents tasks combining datasets, solvers and scorers, with epochs, sample limits and model options. Supports a Python task evaluation option without establishing a successful run or a preferred framework.

title: Andrej Karpathy: LLM Wiki idea file
contribution: Describes separate raw sources, generated Markdown pages and schema conventions, with ingest, query, lint, index and log practices. The source is an abstract idea file, not a runnable service or evidence of accuracy or maintenance cost.
license: No explicit license in the reviewed gist

title: Microsoft Skills: Deep Wiki source-grounded Q&A guidance
contribution: Directs repository answers to actual source files, file-location citations and explicit insufficient-evidence statements. Atlas selectively uses these checks as reading guidance without requiring the plugin or its presentation instructions.

title: AWS Builders Library: safe retries and idempotent APIs
contribution: Describes caller-provided request identifiers, atomic recording with side effects, repeated responses and changed-parameter handling. It does not implement Atlas event processing.

title: Scrum Guide 2020: planning selected work and the Definition of Done
contribution: Describes planning selected backlog items into smaller work and using a Definition of Done. Atlas adapts the planning principle without requiring Scrum or the guide's timeboxes.

title: Google SRE book: release engineering
contribution: Describes reproducible builds, release candidate identity, tests of the release revision, audit trails and rollout considerations in Google's environment. Atlas does not require Google's tooling.

title: Atlassian Confluence Cloud, change history macro
contribution: Documents a change history macro displaying page or live document version number, author, date and comment. This scoped contribution does not establish an approval policy or factual correctness.

title: SEI, Managing Technical Debt with Data-Driven Analysis
publisher: Carnegie Mellon University Software Engineering Institute
contribution: Describes a research approach combining code analysis, architectural analysis and issue tracker data to consolidate and rank candidate technical debt items. It does not validate Atlas categories, a project inventory or an automatic prioritization rule.

title: Google engineering practices, Small CLs
contribution: Describes self-contained changes with related tests and planning how dependent changes will be split. This is published engineering guidance, not a mandatory policy for another repository.

title: Jenkins, Recording tests and artifacts
contribution: Documents publishing generated test reports with junit and retaining artifacts with archiveArtifacts. Failing tests can mark a pipeline unstable, and execution proceeds by default unless configured otherwise. Actual installed plugins, report paths and gates remain project facts.

title: Atlassian Jira Cloud, Configure work item linking
contribution: Documents administrator-controlled work item linking, configurable link types and the Link Work Items permission. This does not create acceptance criteria, prove tenant configuration or authorize writes.

title: Jenkins User Handbook, Pipeline
contribution: Documents a Pipeline definition in a Jenkinsfile that can be committed to source control. It supports assigning CI responsibilities to an inspectable pipeline, not assuming any particular repository has that file or a supported integration.

title: Wikidata: qualifiers, scope and competing values
contribution: Documents qualifier mechanics for contextual scope, validity and time, and representing competing perspectives in Wikidata. Supports only those representation claims, not the fictional holiday example, factual truth of a data assertion or a universal authority policy.

title: GOV.UK: analyse a research session
revision: Published and last updated 2016-05-24, sections Extract observations, Determine findings and Decide actions read 2026-10-15
publisher: GOV.UK Service Manual, User research community
contribution: Distinguishes recorded observations from interpreted findings and proposed actions. Provides a related evidence practice, not a specification for the four Atlas requirement-status labels or proof of a project requirement.

title: Anthropic: multi-agent research delegation and artifact handoffs
contribution: Supports scoped descriptions of explicit subagent objectives, output formats, boundaries and persistent artifact references. This is an inspected production design example, not proof that the proposed Atlas roles improve every task.

title: Jenkins: Pipeline run details and Console Output
contribution: Supports locating a particular Pipeline run in Build History and reading its full Console Output. Does not establish the cause of a failure or configure a Jenkins connection.

title: Bazel: remote action caching and declared inputs
contribution: Supports the build example of actions with explicit inputs, command lines and environment variables, action hashes and cached result metadata. Does not specify a cache implementation for Atlas analysis or guarantee correct reuse of model outputs.

title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook: requirement verification matrix
contribution: Supports Appendix D guidance linking each uniquely identified shall requirement included in the verification matrix to its source document and verification approach. Adaptation to a software brief is an Atlas recommendation, not a claim that NASA rules apply to all projects.

title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook: requirements change impact
contribution: Supports section 6.2.1.2.5 guidance to assess changes against a documented baseline before approval and implementation, plus configuration control of analyses whose inputs can change. Does not prove an impact for any particular software change.
